identity.name: mission
identity.purpose: Mission Control is a local-first coordination application for an ecosystem of AI projects, books, research programmes and commercial work. It is not a library: it is a FastAPI backend (loopback-only) plus a React/Vite single-page UI, with a PostgreSQL operational store. Its user-meaningful job is to answer, in one place:

gaps: No live execution was authorized: no endpoint was called, no server or container was started, no migration was applied, no browser session was run, no model/CLI call was made and no test suite was executed. Every operational_status is therefore bounded at tested-not-demonstrated or source-inspected-only; nothing is verified-working.

The working tree is dirty at HEAD e98884497fd3c34fbb4a89604a9aca587a00bf5c (dirty_tree=true). Findings describe the files as read in the working tree; the clean committed revision may differ, and a git status/diff could not be run under the read-only, no-shell constraint.

API routers were inventoried from route decorators and module headers. Individual route implementations, Pydantic schemas and edge-case branches were sampled rather than read line by line; very large services (workflows/service.py ~2.3k lines, cultivation/service.py ~3k lines, publication/pipeline.py ~1.5k lines, quality/service.py, work_observation/evaluate.py) were characterised from headers, symbol maps and targeted sections.

frontend/src was inspected at the routing/page/feature level (App.tsx, page list, selected components and tests) and used as evidence for backend capabilities. Individual component behaviour and CSS were not exhaustively enumerated; frontend/dist was not built or served.

External engines and their contracts (Next schema, Work CLI, CoCoder artifacts, Worker HTTP/harness, Writer report schema and CLI actions, ALIVE endpoints, Inspect CLI/snapshot, AI Test CLI, OpenCode database, GitHub, Hugo, Praxis proposal format) are outside this repository and were not inspected; their behaviour is described only as Mission Control's client/adapter code and docs state it.

Documentation in docs/ was used for context (MC01/MC09/MC10/MC11/MC-WRITER-01/MC-LIVING-BOOK-01/Praxis/Inspect/Cost/Pipeline reports) but was not treated as proof of implementation; capability evidence cites source and test files. Some docs describe milestone acceptance runs that were not re-verified here.

Scripts under scripts/ are operational helpers (setup/start/stop/dev/test, SQLite->PostgreSQL migration, PG backup, repo-state capture, Git smoke probes, Workbench browser test, prompt generator, acceptance expo02 artifacts). Only the migration utility is represented as a capability component; the rest are not promoted to application capabilities.

Test files are cited as evidence that a test exists; no test result is asserted. The README itself reports environment-dependent failures and one skipped test in earlier full runs, which were not reproduced.
